entries.topic: Are new-version diagnostic logs sufficient to identify provider usage drivers?
facts: Owner asks whether current new-version logs are sufficient for usage-root-cause analysis; this is a review request, not a code/release approval.

Agent FirestoreQuotaGuard aggregates local method/component/hour outcomes and attaches D166_USAGE_AUDIT during existing log seals; these are process-local estimated operations, not actual account or database billable reads.

Android D166UsageAudit records bounded HTTP route family/status/elapsed and error counts only at support bundle boundary; Web runtime-logger has bounded event RAM and resource samples (420-event cap). Neither alone captures complete Firebase provider billing.
Worker/InventoryCore have DO-route and selected SQL-cursor in-isolate bounded diagnostics; restart resets and other Cloudflare Worker/CPU/account operations require provider metrics.
D168 local-first archive schedules Agent and authenticated Web once after 21:45 VN, Android on logout/kick, plus authorized support requests; Drive receipt/archive gaps matter.

D168 historical Apps Script UrlFetch forensic report demonstrated a shared account meter cannot be attributed exactly from Agent logs; after SKU path changed direct Worker, historical request weights cannot be applied blindly.

Need provider-console/project-scope verified readings for Firestore, Cloudflare Worker/DO SQL, Apps Script executions/UrlFetch, and normalized business volumes before claiming exact cost, quota savings or single root cause.
No new instrument, timed polling, code changes or release authorized by this discussion.
entries.next_action: Collect real Agent/Android/Web complete archived logs and provider usage screenshots/exports for comparable shifts, then correlate per-hour costs per online device/agent and per 1,000 business operations in the consolidated D169 analysis; propose only Owner-gated adjustments.

entries.topic: Consolidated D169 analysis of 14 Oct Android/Agent/Web archived logs, v110/v132 and canonical source; proposals only
facts: Drive scoped Beta 2026-10-14 archive contains Android logout-boundary bundles, Agent checkpoint/error/session logs and a Web bundle; some files archive earlier event dates. Repeated/archive-cumulative counters must not be summed as billed usage.
Android version distribution is mixed (vc106-vc110) although signed vc110 release exists; latest file for an individual device does not establish current install after the archive boundary.

Android result receipt endpoint reports clustered RESULT_ACK_NOT_FOUND HTTP 404. InventoryCore result-stage SQL checks BOTH event id and actor user id; absent row produces 404. Root cause (missing row, mismatched account, stages RECEIVED/DISPLAYED/ACK, or stale event) is not yet proven.

PickerController and CriticalOverlayService dismiss their visible result UI before async ACK and persist owner-scoped pending acknowledgements; an HTTP 404 cannot alone prove touchscreen/overlay hang. Keep distinct from long, unscrollable contact message.

Agent error bundles include RTDB auth/timeout fallbacks, DNS/transport failures, WMS WebView2/DevTools failures, deferred SKU sync, Agent presence reconcile failures, and Apps Script UrlFetch daily-quota errors. A source-backed D160 Usage panel continues automatic 15-minute gateway requests, subject to role gate; shared account quota cannot be attributed exactly from logs.

Agent current source VERSION is v132 and one active Agent log proves startup v132; Web source is 3.1.1. Archived Web bundle reports a 06:00 scheduled reason while current main runtime-logger schedules after 21:45, indicating a deployed/cached build divergence or archival provenance requiring verification.

Presence source supports Picklist fallback and tombstones but issues can arise from stale generations, event ordering, fallback retention or UI refresh. Presence version read from app_version may be absent; no isolated root cause proven.
Firestore picker-contact-open-query returns up to 100 legacy documents; significant read estimates occur in the Agent's process-local ledger. Only provider meters determine billed charges.

Current D168 network helper already supports approved saved Wi-Fi profiles, single-shot Worker probes, user permission and restoration; 401/403/429 and service failures are not eligible for blind network switching.

Canonical RBAC already grants PICKPACK_ADMIN certain Picker lifecycle and SKU capabilities but retains Inventory ADMIN-only conflict override and ROOT-only privileged lifecycle; need verify each Web/API operation before proposing any role expansion.

All evidence analyzed in memory via connected Drive and GitHub; no raw logs, person identifiers, SKU, credentials or support-bundle contents committed to this public repo. No executable, runtime, Stable, domain or release change.
